subject: Re: chromosome seems to be removed when I run sequenza.extract

messages.author: dad6980b76d10753
messages.subject: Re: chromosome seems to be removed when I run sequenza.extract
parts:
Hi,

it can be that the sorting of the chromosomes of the 2 mpileups and the GC window file are not compatible. This may result in a seqz file that have only fewer chromosomes (depending on the overlaps of the chromosomes during the parsing of the 3 files).

To overcome the issue, you could manually generate seqz files for each chromosome and then merge the various files afterwards.

If you are interested, I also developed a general workflow framework (it’s just a python library) that implements a sequenza pipeline. It generates the seqz files for each chromosome and merge the resulting files in a unique seqz file, so it should bypass your current problem. If you think this would be useful I can expand on that...


Francesco

On 3 Aug 2017, at 04.31, BinBaek <a01039...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi.

I'm trying to run a "sequenza", but something is wrong.
Before I made a pileup file, the bam file has chromosome 1 - 22 and X, Y but when I run a sequenza.extract, there is only one chromosome(chr1).



> test <- sequenza.extract("out_PAAD_small.seqz.gz")
Processing chr1: 42 variant calls; 2970 heterozygous positions; 357535 homozygous positions.
> test$chromosomes
[1] "chr1"


I don't know what happend. Could anyone let me know how can I get all chrs as an output?


--

messages.subject: Re: chromosome seems to be removed when I run sequenza.extract
parts:
Hi.

There are some problems when I ran 'sequenza-utils.py pileup2seqz' since the size of out.seqz.gz file was smaller than others.
So I could solve the problem by re run pileup2seqz.:)
Still, really thank you for your kindly answering.

Can I ask you one more thing?

when sequenza finds the copy number of A allele and B allele, does it consider the neighbor SNVs of mutations?

I would like to know the mutations were appeared after amplification of alleles or not.
But It seems to difficult to know it with outputs of sequenza.

for example, when the number of mutation is 1, the copy number of A allele is 2, and B allele is 1.
There can be two possible interpretation.

one is AA' B  => mutation was in A allele and occured after amplification of A allele.
second is AA B' => mutation was occured in B allele, and B was not amplified. 

Can I know which interpretation was right with the outputs of sequenza?
If sequenza considered the SNVs, I thought I could know by comparing SNVs of normal and tumor of that position which has mutation.

Thank you.
Bin.
